anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L1 simplified configuration is a fixed 5x5x3 isometric voxel scene. Rotation changes depth order and mining changes the available voxel inventory, so it tests static spatial reasoning and a short state-dependent extraction sequence, but it has no moving traffic or continuous vehicle control. Courtesy Junction at d4/full adds continuous steering and pedal control, autonomous moving agents, collision geometry, and terminal off-road/contact risk, placing it clearly above this low anchor.

The grader replays rotations and raycast mining, durability, hazards, inventory, and the final state.
The solver uses the ordinary rotation/click UI while consulting privileged solution data, so it is implementation wiring evidence rather than the visual burden.

anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L2 full configuration asks for one active cursor search and one accepted click: moving the lens reveals a target amid decoys/noise, then the grader checks click distance. There is no persistent physical route, autonomous actor, or state-dependent sequence after the click. Courtesy Junction requires maintaining a moving vehicle and re-evaluating traffic gaps throughout the drive, so even d1 is above this anchor.

anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L3 full configuration is the closest continuous-control anchor: a ball with momentum must pass ordered lamps and holes around walls and hazards under analog drag, with replayed physics. Courtesy d4/full has a comparable continuous trajectory burden but replaces fixed board hazards and ordered waypoints with three interacting traffic approaches and a turn-dependent departure goal; the 9 responsive cars make d4 more than the L3 low/medium setting while remaining in the same broad continuous-control family.

anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L4 full configuration is a discrete 18x11 route through five ordered gates, scanners, and hidden die orientation. Its burden is symbolic path planning and remembering/using orientation across rolls. Courtesy d4/full is a different L4 expression: a live continuous trajectory with responsive traffic and collision-sensitive timing instead of hidden orientation. Both have changing state and multi-step decisions, so d4 fits the L4 band without needing to resemble the dice task.

anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L5 simplified configuration requires exactly four valid adjacent swaps whose cascades/refills produce an exact score while avoiding forbidden licorice. Each accepted swap changes the board and future options, and grading checks the full state-changing receipt. Courtesy d5 adds traffic density, speed, and narrower geometry, but its route is a fixed reactive driving problem without an exact combinatorial score target or a required state-changing search witness. Source evidence therefore supports d5 as high L4, not an automatic L5.

visible_baseline_solution: From screenshots, start the engine and read the 2D 900x520 scene: the yellow car's pose, road edges and lane markings, the striped left/right departure goal, traffic-car positions and directions, and visible brake lights. Use successive observations to judge which cars are slowing and choose steering plus throttle, coast, or brake while keeping the car body on the road. Follow the visible turn to place the entire car inside the striped goal, then file the delivery. Full uses held arrow keys with release to neutralize an axis; Simplified uses persistent steering/pedal buttons. Collision, crossing the road edge, or timeout terminates the drive, so there is no ordinary in-run recovery after a bad trajectory; a successful run must end in the arrived state and submit its exact physical transcript.

baseline_judgment.rationale: The d4/full baseline is a real continuous driving problem: three approaches produce nine moving cars, drivers react to predicted conflicts and gaps, the yellow car has acceleration, braking, heading and rectangular collision geometry, and either turn must be completed inside the goal. This is materially above the static/spatial L1 mine and one-click L2 constellation task, and it is at least comparable to the continuous L3 tilt board. Its combination of ongoing motor control and responsive traffic fits the approved L4 Blind Dice Courier band, although the burden is physical/temporal rather than symbolic route memory. It remains below the approved L5 Exact-Change Candy Cascade's exact multi-step state-changing score search. No source-supported reversal, unused difficulty knob, mode bypass, or impossible baseline was found.

concise_summary: Keep Courtesy Junction at the approved L4/full baseline. D4 is a continuous 2D driving task with nine responsive traffic cars, turn-dependent routing, collision/off-road terminal states, and exact physical replay. The five profiles are source-wise ordered in both interaction modes; d5 is a high-L4 candidate rather than a source-proven L5.
limitations: No human or screenshot-agent calibration was performed or available in the reviewed source.
No browser, generation, test, grader, or exported-verifier runtime check was performed; runtime_checks_performed is intentionally empty for the parent audit.
Historical preservation could not be established without a pre-controls implementation or seed fixture.
Absolute profile labels, especially the d5 L4/L5 boundary, remain source-based.
